name: DeLorean DMC-12
description:
The DeLorean DMC-12 was the only model built by John DeLorean's DeLorean Motor Company, made in Dunmurry, Northern Ireland, for the American market from 1981 to 1983. Giugiaro styled it, Lotus engineered it: a steel backbone chassis under a glass-fibre tub clad in brushed stainless steel panels, with gull-wing doors and all-independent suspension. About 9,000 were made before the company collapsed.

The engine hangs behind the rear axle: the 2.85-litre PRV V6 (Peugeot-Renault-Volvo) with Bosch K-Jetronic injection, 130 hp at 5,500 rpm and 207 Nm at 2,750 rpm in US trim, through a Renault five-speed transaxle on a 3.44 final drive and an open differential. With 62% of its 1,290 kg on the rear wheels, 195/60 R14 tyres in front and 235/60 R15 behind, it is a gentle understeerer that was never as fast as it looked - the factory claimed 130 mph and 8.8 s to 60, Road & Track measured 110 mph and 10.5 s.

It became a film icon as the time machine of the Back to the Future trilogy.

Model and original physics by BCRC Mods (https://www.patreon.com/bcrc). Physics corrected to factory specification.
